title_en: Wang Jianhua et al. v. Wang Rufan — dispute over inheritance
keywords_en: Civil; Inheritance dispute; First instance; Basic People's Court; Guangdong Province; Natural person; Inheritance Law; Marriage Law; Civil Procedure Law; Equality of inheritance rights; Loss of inheritance rights due to abuse; Failure to fulfill support obligations; Determination of community property of spouses; Inheritance rights of stepchildren; Partial support; Remarriage; Estate division; Pre-marital property; Community property of spouses; Gift; Abuse; Hua et al. (five persons) v. Wang Rufan — inheritance dispute
full_text_en:
Wang Jianhua et al. v. Wang Rufan — inheritance dispute

Plaintiffs: Wang Jianhua, male, 48 years old, employee, residing in Hong Kong.
Plaintiff: Wang Qianghua, male, 52 years old, worker, residing in Shanghai.
Plaintiff: Wang Qihua, female, 49 years old, teacher, residing in Shanghai.
Plaintiff: Wang Shunhua, female, 46 years old, worker, residing in Shanghai.
Plaintiff: Wang Youhua, female, 43 years old, unemployed, residing in Hong Kong.
Defendant: Wang Rufan, female, 58 years old, retired teacher, residing in Shenzhen.
Third party: Wang Yin, female, 35 years old, teacher, residing in Hong Kong.

Plaintiffs Wang Jianhua, Wang Qianghua, Wang Qihua, Wang Shunhua, and Wang Youhua filed an action with the Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, against defendant Wang Rufan and third party Wang Yin concerning an inheritance dispute.

The plaintiffs alleged: The defendant Wang Rufan married the decedent Wang Jianing because she coveted his property. After marriage, the defendant frequently abused the decedent. When the decedent fell ill, she did not send him to the hospital for treatment, but left him to suffer in pain at home. It was not until the decedent was critically ill that the defendant informed the plaintiff Wang Jianhua. When Wang Jianhua took the decedent to Hong Kong for treatment, the defendant took the opportunity to take from Wang Jianhua the keys to the safety deposit box the decedent had kept in Hong Kong, and removed the decedent's cash and stocks. After the decedent's death, the defendant occupied or rented out four properties purchased by the decedent before marriage. When the plaintiffs consulted with her regarding the inheritance, the defendant ignored them, intending to monopolize the property that the plaintiffs were entitled to. The plaintiffs requested the court to rule by law that the defendant had forfeited her right of inheritance, that the entire estate of the decedent and the rental income from the decedent's properties obtained by the defendant should be inherited by the plaintiffs, and that the defendant bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendant and third party argued: Among the properties in dispute, part was property given by the decedent Wang Jianing to the defendant during his lifetime, and part was property purchased with joint contributions from Wang Jianing and the third party. This portion of property is not part of Wang Jianing's estate. Furthermore, it was only after Wang Jianing married the defendant that he repaid the pre-marital housing loans; this should be regarded as using the marital community property to repay individual loans, and should be deducted from the estate. The defendant does not object to the plaintiffs inheriting Wang Jianing's estate as first-order statutory successors. However, each plaintiff has the ability and conditions to provide support, but for a long time has not assumed any support obligations towards Wang Jianing. Therefore, they should receive no share or a smaller share in the inheritance. The defendant was registered in marriage with Wang Jianing, lived with him in his later years, relied on each other, and treated each other with respect. She should not only inherit Wang Jianing's estate as a first-order statutory successor, but should also receive a larger share according to law. At a time when Wang Jianing was lonely and destitute in his later years, only the third party, out of humanitarianism, gave Wang Jianing HKD 500 monthly as living expenses. After the defendant married Wang Jianing, the third party and her brother Wang Ming, as stepchildren of Wang Jianing, assumed the obligation of supporting Wang Jianing. Therefore, they should also inherit the estate as first-order statutory successors.

The Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen found through trial: Plaintiffs Wang Jianhua, Wang Qianghua, Wang Qihua, Wang Shunhua, and Wang Youhua are all legitimate children of the decedent Wang Jianing and his former wife. In July 1989, Wang Jianing remarried the defendant Wang Rufan. There were no children from this marriage. The third party Wang Yin and her brother Wang Ming are both legitimate children of Wang Rufan and her former husband. Wang Yin moved to Hong Kong to settle in July 1986; Wang Ming went to Japan for study in February 1989. On June 1, 1991, Wang Jianing died of illness in Hong Kong. Since he left no will, a dispute arose between the plaintiffs and the defendant over the division of the estate, leading to this lawsuit.

The decedent Wang Jianing purchased one unit of property, Unit D, 16th Floor, Block 2, Dexing Building, Jianshe Road, Shenzhen, in 1985, valued at HKD 210,903. In July 1987, Wang Jianing purchased one unit of property, Unit H, 15th Floor, Block 1, Haifengyuan Hengshan Pavilion, Renmin South Road, Shenzhen, valued at HKD 316,031. On July 30 of that year, he donated half of the title to this property to the defendant Wang Rufan by notarization. In April 1988, Wang Jianing and the third party Wang Yin jointly purchased one unit of property, Unit B, 2nd Floor, Block 1, Oriental Garden Villa, Huaqiao Cheng, Shenzhen, valued at HKD 1,010,907, and also purchased one unit of property, Unit E, 2nd Floor, Block 2, Oriental Garden Villa, valued at HKD 1,035,146. At the time of purchase, a loan of HKD 600,000 was taken out, which has been repaid jointly by Wang Jianing and Wang Yin.

After marriage, the decedent Wang Jianing and the defendant Wang Rufan resided at Unit B, 2nd Floor, Block 1, Oriental Garden Villa. During this period, they purchased household items including four Mitsubishi air conditioners, one Pearl River brand piano, one Hitachi 20-inch color television, and one telephone. Unit E, 2nd Floor, Block 2, Oriental Garden Villa was rented out from March 1, 1991, to January 30, 1992, with monthly rent of HKD 4,000 received by Wang Rufan.

The Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen held: Plaintiffs Wang Jianhua, Wang Qianghua, Wang Qihua, Wang Shunhua, and Wang Youhua are all biological children of the decedent Wang Jianing, and the defendant Wang Rufan is the wife of Wang Jianing. Pursuant to Article 10, Paragraph 1, and Article 13, Paragraph 1, of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, they are all first-order statutory successors of Wang Jianing with equal inheritance rights. The plaintiffs' claim that Wang Rufan abused Wang Jianing and should forfeit her inheritance rights, and Wang Rufan's claim that the plaintiffs failed to fulfill their support obligations and should receive no share or a smaller share, are not supported due to the absence of corresponding evidence, in accordance with Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. As for the claim by the third party and on behalf of her brother Wang Ming to inherit the estate as stepchildren of Wang Jianing, since both had already moved to Hong Kong and Japan to reside before Wang Jianing married Wang Rufan, and there is insufficient evidence to establish that a support relationship had been formed between them and Wang Jianing, pursuant to Article 10, Paragraph 3, of the Inheritance Law, they cannot become successors of Wang Jianing.

The defendant Wang Rufan married the decedent Wang Jianing in July 1989. The household items such as air conditioners, telephone, piano, and color television purchased after the marriage, and the rental income from the property received from March 1, 1991, to June 1, 1991, are property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship. Pursuant to Article 13, Paragraph 1, of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, they constitute marital community property, with half of the title belonging to Wang Jianing. Wang Rufan and Wang Jianing had been married for a relatively short period; after marriage, Wang Rufan stayed at home resting and did not engage in any operational work or have income. When Wang Jianing repaid the pre-marital housing loan, he used funds from his own account in Hong Kong. This portion of funds was Wang Jianing's pre-marital individual property and cannot be considered marital community property. As for the property of Unit H, 15th Floor, Block 1, Haifengyuan Hengshan Pavilion, after Wang Jianing purchased it, he donated half of its title to Wang Rufan by notarization. This donation is valid, and Wang Jianing only owns the title to the other half. The two properties, Unit B, 2nd Floor, Block 1, Oriental Garden Villa, and Unit E, 2nd Floor, Block 2, Oriental Garden Villa, were both purchased with joint contributions from Wang Jianing and the third party Wang Yin; Wang Jianing has a half title. All of the above properties belonging to Wang Jianing were his pre-marital individual property, with a total value of HKD 1,391,945. After Wang Jianing's death, this portion of property, together with the property belonging to Wang Jianing from the marital community property and the rental income continued to be received by Wang Rufan after Wang Jianing's death on June 1, 1991, constitutes the estate of Wang Jianing, to be inherited by the five plaintiffs and the defendant.

The defendant Wang Rufan lived together with Wang Jianing during his lifetime until his death. Pursuant to Article 13, Paragraph 3, of the Inheritance Law, she may receive a larger share of the estate. Accordingly, on the basis of finding the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, the Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen mediated this case in accordance with Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. On March 31, 1992, the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement:

1. One unit of property, Unit E, 2nd Floor, Block 2, Oriental Garden Villa, Huaqiao Cheng, Shenzhen, shall belong to the third party Wang Yin.

2. Two units of property, Unit D, 6th Floor, Block 2, Dexing Building, Jianshe Road, Shenzhen, and Unit H, 15th Floor, Haifengyuan Hengshan Pavilion, Renmin Road, Shenzhen, shall belong to the defendant Wang Rufan.

3. One unit of property, Unit B, 2nd Floor, Block 1, Oriental Garden Villa, Huaqiao Cheng, Shenzhen, shall be jointly owned by the plaintiffs Wang Jianhua, Wang Qianghua, Wang Qihua, Wang Shunhua, and Wang Youhua.

4. One Mitsubishi air conditioner, one Hitachi 20-inch color television, the rental income from Unit E, 2nd Floor, Block 2, Oriental Garden Villa, and the daily household items used by the defendant Wang Rufan and Wang Jianing after marriage shall all belong to Wang Rufan. Three Mitsubishi air conditioners, one telephone, and one Pearl River brand piano shall be jointly owned by the plaintiffs Wang Jianhua, Wang Qianghua, Wang Qihua, Wang Shunhua, and Wang Youhua.

5. Regarding the estate and debts of the decedent Wang Jianing in Hong Kong, the parties agree to apply to the relevant authorities in Hong Kong for disposition.

The case acceptance fee and property appraisal fee shall be borne one-third each by the plaintiffs, the defendant, and the third party.
